A few steps down and you're on a private beach with a pier reaching nearly 400 meters into the sea — Rayong Resort Hotel is a 4-star beach resort sitting on the tip of Laem Tarn in Phe Sub-district, right next to Khao Laem Ya–Mu Ko Samet National Park · What most people talk about is the private beachfront location, where every room has a balcony looking out to the sea and the islands, plus three outdoor pools, a spa, and a spot near Ban Phe pier where you can catch a boat to Koh Samet in about 30 minutes · Around 130 rooms, from about THB 3,000/night, scored 8.7 from 91 reviews on Trip.com, and TripAdvisor rates it 4.0/5, ranked #1 of 6 hotels in Phe Sub-district

body.html: Who Rayong Resort Hotel is right for — the shortest way to put it: Rayong Resort Hotel is a beach resort for people who want to fall asleep to the sound of the waves and wake up to the sea the moment they open the balcony door · It's not a hotel in Rayong town built around easy shopping, dining, and getting around, and it's not a brand-new luxury resort selling polish in every square inch · Instead it's a large seafront resort set on the tip of Laem Tarn in Phe Sub-district, next to Khao Laem Ya–Mu Ko Samet National Park · Open since 1988, it's one of Rayong's old-guard resorts that many Thai families know well and keep coming back to · It's still going strong today, with TripAdvisor ranking it #1 of 6 hotels in Phe Sub-district at 4.0/5 from over 268 reviews, and Trip.com rating it 8.7/10 · Real reviews line up on who fits here: families who want the kids to swim in the sea and the pools all they like, couples after some privacy by the beach, and groups or companies coming for a retreat who want a seaside setting — more than people hunting for a freshly designed room or a downtown location · Another group that says they were won over uses this place as a base before or after the boat to Koh Samet, since it's near Ban Phe pier and gives you the mainland sea in a quieter setting than on the island · You could say it's a resort that leans fully into "a private sea without crossing to the island," and the trade-off is that the buildings and some of the rooms are a fair age, which is worth setting expectations on from the start

Location and getting there — this is Rayong Resort Hotel's number-one selling point, no question · The resort sits at 186 Moo 1, Phe Sub-district, on the tip of Laem Tarn jutting out into the sea, right next to Khao Laem Ya–Mu Ko Samet National Park, only about 0.5 km from the Khao Laem Ya viewpoint · Being on the tip of the cape means you get the sea on nearly every side and a private beach of your own, which is rare for a resort in Rayong · Onward travel is convenient if you want to head to the island: Ban Phe pier is only about 3 km away, and the boat from Ban Phe pier to Koh Samet takes about 30 minutes, so many people use this as a stopover before or after going to the island · From Bangkok it's about a 2-hour drive via the motorway, and about 50 km past Pattaya · One key note that reviews agree on is that the privacy of the location comes at the cost of being out of the way — many of the restaurants and convenience stores nearby close early, around 9 PM, and if you want to head out for food or supplies you may have a fair drive ahead. Anyone without their own car should plan for this in advance, or mainly eat at the resort

"You open the balcony and the sea is right there. In the morning you walk down to the long pier and the photos come out gorgeous, and the kids can splash in the sea and the pool all day — the privacy is what I love most. But I'll admit heading out for food in the evening is a bit of a hassle."

Room types and decor — Rayong Resort Hotel has about 130 rooms, and the shared charm here is that nearly every room has a private balcony looking out to the sea and nearby islands · The popular entry-level room is the Junior Suite, with a choice of King or Twin beds, from about THB 3,095 · Step up to the Deluxe Sea View at about 36 sqm on floors 5–7 for a wider sea view · There's a Deluxe Triple at 36 sqm for three people or a small family on the 4th floor · and the top room is the Premier Suite Sea View with a King bed, putting extra emphasis on space and the view · The decor is classic seaside-resort style, leaning on comfort and function over modern design, with air-con, satellite TV, and tea/coffee facilities in every room · The thing to say plainly, going by real reviews, is that some of the rooms and furniture show their age and are starting to feel dated given the year it opened, since the resort has been running since 1988, and a few rooms feel compact and due for a refresh · What makes up for it is the sea view that opens out from almost every balcony, a detail many reviews say lets you forget about the age · If you care about the view and a room's freshness, ask for a high floor or a recently renovated room when you book, since the standard varies quite a bit between floors and zones

Facilities, pools, and spa — the most-talked-about highlight at Rayong Resort Hotel is the private beach and the pier reaching about 380 meters into the sea, which has become a popular spot for photos and strolls in the morning and evening · The resort has three outdoor pools spread across the grounds, so guests don't have to compete for space even when it's busy, and kids have plenty of room to swim · For unwinding there's the Daovadeung Retreat spa, offering massage and treatments in a seafront setting · There's a good range of water and recreation activities too — kayaking, table tennis, billiards, and karaoke · On top of that there's a fitness room, free parking, and Wi-Fi in the common areas · What gives this place an edge for big groups is a convention center for up to about 500 people, making it popular for seafront seminars and banquets · To be straight about it, the beach and water on this side are the natural shoreline of Ban Phe bay, and at times reviews mention the cleanliness of the beach and debris washing in with the waves depending on the season, which is more about the area than the resort's own upkeep — but it's worth knowing before you expect the clear white sand of an island

Food and bars — the resort has more than one restaurant and bar, serving both Thai and international food, with a seafront seating area that's especially nice in the evening · Breakfast is Western-style, served from 7:00–10:00 AM, and it's a spot many reviews praise for the atmosphere of eating while looking out at the sea in the morning, more than for the variety you'd get from a city-hotel buffet · There's a seafront bar and karaoke for anyone who wants to socialize at night · Since the location is fairly private and the places outside close early, many reviews suggest you plan to have dinner mainly at the resort, especially without your own car · If you want a change of scenery, it's a short drive into Ban Phe market or the pier area, which have fresh seafood restaurants and local treats to choose from · Overall, the food at Rayong Resort Hotel isn't a showstopper, but it's a solid add-on in the context of a seafront resort built around eating and staying within the grounds, and the real strength is the atmosphere of dining with a sea view rather than the menu itself

Service — service is another point that earns steady praise in real reviews · Plenty of staff get mentioned as friendly, smiling, and attentive, especially the front-desk team and the seafront restaurant staff · There's a 24-hour front desk and a shuttle service on some routes · For seminar groups and large families, the team is praised for coordinating activities and seafront banquets · But to be fair, since it's a large resort that's been open a long time, some voices in the reviews say the speed and detail of service aren't equally consistent everywhere, especially when the resort is full or there's a big tour group · On the whole it's still warm service in the style of a Thai family resort, a charm that brings many guests back for repeat stays

Voices from real reviews (praise and criticism) — pulled together from Trip.com, TripAdvisor, Booking.com, and Wongnai, and the picture is fairly consistent · On the praise side: the private, naturally beautiful beachfront location, every room having a sea-view balcony, the private beach and the long pier that photographs well, multiple pools good for families, friendly staff, and the atmosphere of having breakfast with a sea view · One Thai-language review on Wongnai describes it as "probably the most private here, with the most beautiful nature" and "a hotel on the hill, embraced by nature" · On the criticism side: the most-mentioned point is the age of the buildings and rooms — the resort has been open since 1988, and some rooms feel small and due for a refresh · Next is how out-of-the-way the location is, with shops and restaurants outside closing early around 9 PM, making it hard to head out without a car · And there's the cleanliness of the beach and debris washing in with the sea at certain times of year · Most of these criticisms are about the age of the buildings and the natural state of the area more than problems that keep people from returning, and many still rate it highly because they see the privacy and sea views as worth these limits

"The sea view from the balcony is gorgeous, the kids love the pool, the staff are lovely · My only gripe is the rooms are getting old and some fittings are dated to the hotel's age. Next time I'll ask for a high-floor room that's just been renovated instead."

Price and value — the entry-level Junior Suite starts at about THB 3,000/night in the normal range, and can climb to around THB 4,300–4,500+ during high season, long weekends, or the Saturdays and Sundays when people flock to the sea · The Deluxe Sea View and Premier Suite Sea View sit in a higher range depending on size and the view angle · Compared with other Rayong beach resorts, Rayong Resort Hotel feels like good value for its location and beachfront privacy at an affordable price, especially counting the private beach, multiple pools, and a sea-view balcony in every room — things newer resorts in the same price range often don't fully match · But if you compare it to a recently opened resort focused on polished, designed rooms, this place may look at a disadvantage on freshness · The bottom line: if you value "the sea view and privacy" over "how new the room is," every baht you pay comes back worth it

Things to know before you book — a few things make the stay smoother · One, if you care about a room's freshness and view, say so when you book and ask for a high floor (Deluxe Sea View on floors 5–7) or a recently renovated room, since the standard varies by zone · Two, the location is fairly private and the places outside close early, so have your own car or plan to have dinner at the resort · Three, if you're coming to catch a boat to Koh Samet, Ban Phe pier is only about 3 km away — ask the resort about a shuttle or a local taxi in advance · Four, during high season and long weekends rooms fill fast and prices climb, so book ahead and compare prices across several platforms · Five, set the right expectations about the beach — it's the natural shoreline of Ban Phe bay, not the clear white sand of an island, and at times there's debris washing in with the water depending on the season · Six, pick free cancellation while your plans aren't firm, since prices tend to shift with the season

The verdict — going by all the real reviews, Rayong Resort Hotel is the resort that fits best for people who want a private slice of sea on Laem Tarn in Ban Phe on an affordable budget, with a beach and pools where the family can swim all they like · Its location next to Khao Laem Ya, a sea-view balcony in every room, a private beach, a 380-meter pier, and being near Ban Phe pier for the onward boat to Koh Samet give it a charm a city resort can't · If you're after a flawless, freshly designed room, or a location where you can step out to restaurants and food easily all night, this may not be the answer, and you should look at a hotel in central Rayong or a recently opened resort instead · But for a beach trip where you want privacy, a sea view from every room, and the warm atmosphere of a family resort at a price worth paying — Rayong Resort Hotel answers that well, and it's why it keeps holding the top spot in Phe Sub-district

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Rayong Resort Hotel

faq.q: Where is Rayong Resort Hotel · how do you get to Koh Samet?
faq.a: The resort is at 186 Moo 1, Phe Sub-district, on the tip of Laem Tarn, next to Khao Laem Ya–Mu Ko Samet National Park, about 0.5 km from the Khao Laem Ya viewpoint · Ban Phe pier is only about 3 km away, with a boat to Koh Samet in about 30 minutes · From Bangkok it's about a 2-hour drive

faq.q: Does Rayong Resort Hotel have a private beach and a pool?
faq.a: Yes · the highlights are a private beach on the tip of Laem Tarn with a pier reaching about 380 meters into the sea and three outdoor pools, good for families bringing kids to swim · There's also the Daovadeung Retreat spa, a fitness room, kayaking, table tennis, billiards, and karaoke

faq.q: What's the starting price at Rayong Resort Hotel · what room types are there?
faq.a: Prices start at about THB 3,000/night for a Junior Suite in the normal range · There's a Deluxe Sea View at 36 sqm on floors 5–7, a Deluxe Triple for three people, and the top-tier Premier Suite Sea View · Nearly every room has a sea-view balcony · During high season and long weekends prices climb to around THB 4,300–4,500+, so compare several platforms before you book

faq.q: Who is Rayong Resort Hotel right for?
faq.a: It's a great fit for families who want the kids to swim in the sea and the pools, couples after some privacy by the beach, and seminar groups who want a seaside setting · It suits people who value the sea view and privacy over a room's freshness or a downtown location · If you're after a flawless, brand-new room or a location where you can walk out for food easily, a hotel in central Rayong may suit you better

faq.q: How old are the rooms at Rayong Resort Hotel · which room should you ask for?
faq.a: Many reviews agree the resort has been open since 1988, so some buildings and rooms show their age and a few are fairly small · We'd suggest asking for a high-floor Deluxe Sea View (floors 5–7) or a recently renovated room when you book, since the standard varies quite a bit between floors and zones, and the sea view from the balcony goes a long way toward making up for the age

faq.q: Staying at Rayong Resort Hotel, is it convenient to find food outside?
faq.a: The location is fairly private on the tip of the cape · many restaurants and convenience stores nearby close early, around 9 PM, so heading out in the evening is a hassle without your own car · We'd suggest planning to have dinner mainly at the resort, or driving into Ban Phe market about 3 km away, which has fresh seafood restaurants and local treats to choose from
